title: Workplace-monitoring co-governance, centralization, and bypass stress test
governing_question: Does APC-01's R6 design survive the strongest observed workplace co-governance control when technical architecture centralizes authority, monitoring is framed as capability rather than active use, systems update or migrate, representative bodies become more remote from local workers, and deletion, compensation, exit, and value rights remain separate?

systems.represented_population: Approximately 1,300 employees in a blood-donation-services group
systems.technical_function: Visitor posts on an employer-operated Facebook page exposed information about employee behavior and performance.
systems.representative_body: Konzernbetriebsrat constituted through lower-level employee-representative bodies
systems.observed_control: The monitoring function had to be disabled unless the council consented or the conciliation committee supplied a substitute decision.
systems.largest_limit: The broader page could continue; the decision did not establish individual veto, platform-purpose authority, deletion, compensation, public or worker ownership, or value recovery.

systems.represented_population: Employees using an enterprise Office 365 environment across multiple establishments
systems.technical_function: A centrally administered tenant contained monitoring-capable functions whose implementation could not be separated by local establishment.
systems.representative_body: Central works council rather than a local works council
systems.observed_control: The court confirmed co-determination and assigned competence to the central body because the technical architecture made the issue company-wide.
systems.largest_limit: The final agreement, implementation conditions, local-worker influence, actual system change, telemetry access, deletion, compensation, and outcomes are not public in the source set.

systems.technical_function: Email software could generate information concerning employee behavior or performance.
systems.observed_control: Co-determination applied and cessation could be sought for unagreed use; the council had exercised co-determination in the specific case.
systems.largest_limit: The decision did not establish a general works-council right to compel third-party deletion, an individual veto, or authority over every downstream use.

systems.represented_population: Employees whose communications could be heard by supervisors through a headset system
systems.technical_function: Supervisors could listen to employee communications even though the conversations were not recorded.
systems.observed_control: The court treated real-time listening capacity as technical monitoring subject to co-determination despite the absence of recording.
systems.largest_limit: The decision does not establish success of every injunction, data rights where no data are retained, individual refusal, compensation, or platform-purpose control.

domain_adapter.name: Worker Monitoring Constitution
domain_adapter.purpose: Apply APC-01 to workplace systems that can observe, infer, score, record, listen to, classify, route, discipline, schedule, reward, exclude, or otherwise make workers and their labor actionable.
covered_actions: introduction or material update of technical monitoring capability
communications, content, location, biometric, productivity, performance, behavior, safety, scheduling, access, or risk monitoring
telemetry, analytics, scoring, profiling, prediction, anomaly detection, recommendation, or automated management
cloud, platform, SaaS, device, headset, email, social-media, collaboration, HR, security, or operations systems with monitoring capacity
new purpose, new data source, new recipient, new threshold, new model, new integration, new retention rule, or new disciplinary use
outsourcing, centralization, cross-border hosting, vendor support, migration, and successor tools
workplace_invariants: Monitoring capability, not only actual use or recording, can trigger constitutional review where the system is objectively capable of observing behavior or performance.
A product update, new telemetry, changed default, new integration, new model, or changed purpose retriggers notice, evidence, pause, and co-governance review.
Employer procurement, cloud configuration, vendor default, security label, or workflow framing cannot remove a monitoring function from coverage when the practical effect is materially equivalent.

The employer must disclose architecture, modules, defaults, configuration, data flows, telemetry, users, roles, thresholds, model behavior, retention, support access, disciplinary uses, and alternatives before introduction or material change.
Co-determination must bind the introduction and use of the covered function; consultation, information, ethics review, policy publication, or post-deployment feedback is insufficient.
Collective representative authority and individual worker rights are complementary and distinct; one may not erase the other.
Where technical indivisibility shifts competence to a central representative body, local and minority workers retain direct petition, information, dissent, removal, and independent-review routes.
A central body must document why the system is technically indivisible and why local authority cannot remain concurrent or delegated for local uses and consequences.

Representative selection, term, removal, conflicts, union access, resources, expertise, turnout, minority representation, and communication back to the constituency are part of practical R6 effectiveness.
Emergency or safety deployment must be specific, time-limited, independently reviewable, minimally configured, and unable to become a permanent monitoring route through renewal or delayed bargaining.

A works agreement must include audit, access, correction, minimization, purpose, retention, deletion, grievance, human-review, disciplinary-use, update, suspension, termination, portability, and successor-system clauses where relevant.
Function-level cessation is not complete R4 unless individual records, downstream copies, disciplinary consequences, residual injury, and compensation are addressed.
Co-determination is not complete R5 without viable substitution, worker-governed public or cooperative capacity, migration, and continuity where the system is terminated.
Co-determination is not R7 without a contribution-right-realization-distribution chain covering worker data, labor, risk, error, productivity gains, model learning, IP, savings, or other value.

Workers outside the statutory constituency, including some contractors, agency workers, managers, public-sector workers, platform workers, and workers in establishments without a council, require separately evidenced receiving constitutions rather than assumed coverage.

r_level_tests.required_by_apc: Workers and their accountable representative receive usable notice before introduction, material update, purpose change, or consequential use.
r_level_tests.facebook_observation: The council learned of and challenged the monitoring function, but the case followed operation rather than proving ordinary pre-introduction worker notice.
r_level_tests.centralization_observation: Office 365 litigation identified the competent central body; actual worker notice and local communication are not established by the current record.

r_level_tests.required_by_apc: The representative and worker can inspect architecture, configuration, telemetry, data, model, threshold, users, decisions, updates, downstream copies, and correction and deletion paths.
r_level_tests.facebook_observation: The function was legible enough for judicial classification, but source data, platform behavior, individual posts, downstream records, and deletion are not closed.
r_level_tests.centralization_observation: Office 365 and email cases establish capability and competence while actual tenant configuration, logs, agreements, user access, and downstream correction remain nonpublic or unresolved.

r_level_tests.required_by_apc: Covered introduction or use pauses automatically until consent or a binding substitute decision, with a bounded safety exception.
r_level_tests.facebook_observation: Visitor posts had to remain disabled until consent or a substitute decision existed.
r_level_tests.centralization_observation: The statutory framework makes co-determination binding, but the estate lacks a denominator of systems paused before deployment versus litigated after violation.

r_level_tests.required_by_apc: Binding cessation, correction, deletion, restoration, compensation, disciplinary reversal, and systemic remedy reach employer, vendor, custodians, and downstream uses.
r_level_tests.facebook_observation: The visitor-post monitoring function had to be switched off; broader page, data, individual injury, deletion, compensation, and vendor architecture remained outside the observed remedy.
r_level_tests.centralization_observation: Email-system doctrine supports cessation while BAG 1 ABR 31/19 limits the inference that the council can compel third-party deletion in every circumstance.

r_level_tests.required_by_apc: Workers and institutions can terminate or substitute the system while preserving work, service, evidence, rights, governance, and independent operating capacity.
r_level_tests.facebook_observation: The employer could continue the page without visitor posts, demonstrating functional narrowing rather than full exit or worker-governed substitution.
r_level_tests.centralization_observation: The source set does not provide completed migrations, worker-governed alternatives, continuity, post-exit custody, or successor-tool performance for Office 365, email, or headset systems.

r_level_tests.required_by_apc: An accountable and removable worker-representative constitution can bind purpose, category, threshold, acceptable use, exception, approval, update, suspension, and termination.
r_level_tests.facebook_observation: The representative body could withhold consent to a specific monitoring use and obtain binding cessation.
r_level_tests.centralization_observation: Technical architecture shifted authority to a central council; formal R6 persisted while proximity to local workers and actual agreement terms became less visible.
missing: selection and removal at central level

r_level_tests.required_by_apc: Workers receive enforceable value rights proportionate to labor, data, risk, error, productivity, surveillance burden, model learning, savings, and institutional capacity supplied.
r_level_tests.facebook_observation: Function-level control did not establish ownership, royalties, IP, data dividends, compensation, governance value, or worker-controlled capacity.
r_level_tests.centralization_observation: The source set does not join Office 365, email, or headset monitoring to realized value, productivity gain, vendor learning, worker contribution, or distribution.
missing: worker ownership, royalty, compensation, or distribution

architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.name: centralization_shifts_governance
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.observation: An indivisible central tenant can move competence from local councils to a central works council.
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.risk: Formal co-determination survives while decision-makers become more distant from locally affected workers.
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.required_control: Technical indivisibility proof, local petition and information rights, representative accountability, minority protection, delegated local authority where possible, and independent review.

architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.name: capability_not_recording
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.observation: Monitoring coverage can attach to a system capable of real-time listening even when no conversation is recorded.
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.risk: Employers and vendors may reframe monitoring as ephemeral, safety-related, passive, optional, or unrecorded to avoid governance.
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.required_control: Functional-equivalence review based on capability, access, inference, action, and worker consequence rather than storage alone.

architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.name: product_update_and_purpose_drift
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.observation: Cloud and platform products can gain new modules, telemetry, analytics, integrations, and defaults after the original agreement.
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.risk: A static agreement may legitimize future monitoring that was never actually negotiated.
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.required_control: Version registry, material-change trigger, update freeze, recurring review, rollback, audit, and renewed consent.

architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.name: representative_capture_and_absence
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.observation: The mechanism depends on an existing competent council with sufficient resources and accountability.
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.risk: Workers without a council, contractors, minority groups, remote workers, or workers represented by a captured or distant body may lack equivalent power.
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.required_control: Direct rights floor, formation support, union and expert access, conflicts, removal, minority appeal, and independent counter-sovereign.

architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.name: remedy_and_value_gap
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.observation: A council can stop use without necessarily controlling deletion, compensation, exit, ownership, IP, or distribution.
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.risk: The institution learns and retains value while workers receive only future-use conditions.
architecture_and_governance_fault_lines.required_control: Joined R4, R5, and R7 instruments separate from R6 consent.

action_packet_translation.burden_rule: The employer bears the burden to show that a system or change is outside monitoring coverage, necessary, proportionate, minimally configured, and consistent with the binding representative constitution. Ambiguity about capability, configuration, purpose, update, or data flow is resolved against unilateral introduction when the material records are held by the employer or vendor.
action_packet_translation.update_rule: Any material new capability, default, data source, model, threshold, integration, recipient, purpose, retention rule, disciplinary use, or successor tool triggers renewed R1, R2, R3, and R6 review before activation.
action_packet_translation.direct_rights_floor: Collective agreement may strengthen but may not eliminate individual notice, evidence access, correction, grievance, non-retaliation, judicial review, and protection against unlawfully disproportionate monitoring.

cross_system_controls.claim: BAG 1 ABR 7/15 supplies an observed bounded R6 control because a worker representative body could prevent a specific monitoring function from operating without consent or a substitute decision.
cross_system_controls.limit: The case followed a violation and did not create direct individual veto, platform control, deletion, compensation, exit, or value recovery.

cross_system_controls.claim: Office 365 shows that technical centralization can centralize worker governance authority.
cross_system_controls.limit: Central authority remains representative but local influence, actual agreement terms, and operational outcomes are not closed.

cross_system_controls.claim: Headset monitoring shows that absence of recording does not remove a functionally monitoring-capable system from co-governance.
cross_system_controls.limit: Coverage does not itself establish data rights, successful enforcement, individual refusal, or complete remedy.

cross_system_controls.claim: Works-council R6 authority supplies direct individual veto for every affected employee.
cross_system_controls.limit: The mechanism is collective and representative; individual rights must be separately established.

cross_system_controls.claim: Function-level cessation supplies complete R4, R5, and R7.
cross_system_controls.limit: Deletion, compensation, substitution, public or worker capacity, ownership, IP, and value distribution remain distinct.

cross_system_controls.claim: The German R6 mechanism transfers directly to public-sector, platform-worker, contractor, nonunion, and non-German systems.
cross_system_controls.limit: Each transfer requires exact receiving law, representative constitution, deployment, contested decision, enforcement, and observed result.

cross_system_controls.claim: APC-WORK-01 should add direct anti-capture, material-update, functional-equivalence, local-proximity, and R4/R5/R7 requirements to the observed R6 control.
cross_system_controls.limit: Additional requirements may conflict with labor-law competence, bargaining autonomy, trade secrets, security, and operational feasibility and require observed testing.

propositions.claim: German works-council law supplies the strongest current bounded R6 positive control because a representative body can bind introduction and use of qualifying technical monitoring and obtain function-level cessation.
propositions.falsifier: The employer may introduce and use a qualifying monitoring system unilaterally despite a competent council, or the binding order had no operational effect.
propositions.stopping_rule: Keep the claim bounded to covered systems, workers, employers, representative bodies, and jurisdiction.

propositions.claim: Technical centralization can preserve formal R6 while making governance more distant from local workers.
propositions.falsifier: Local workers retain equivalent direct influence, access, authority, and remedy over the centralized system.
propositions.stopping_rule: Measure central and local representation, not merely which body is legally competent.

propositions.claim: Functional monitoring capability can trigger governance even when the system does not record data.
propositions.falsifier: Binding law limits coverage to stored or later retrievable records rather than real-time monitoring capability.
propositions.stopping_rule: Keep monitoring capability, data retention, and downstream evidence rights separate.

propositions.claim: Works-council co-determination gives every affected worker a direct individual veto.
propositions.falsifier: A statute, binding agreement, or observed deployment grants each covered worker an enforceable personal veto or opt-out.
propositions.stopping_rule: Preserve individual and collective constitutional forms separately.

propositions.claim: The observed R6 control supplies complete R4 deletion and compensation, R5 substitution, and R7 value recovery.
propositions.falsifier: A complete deployment record closes worker data, injury, deletion, compensation, system migration, worker capacity, contribution, residual rights, realization, and distribution through the same constitution.
propositions.stopping_rule: Do not allow one R-level to self-supply another.

propositions.claim: The German mechanism transfers to other workers and jurisdictions without additional proof.
propositions.falsifier: Matched receiving jurisdictions repeatedly lack binding authority, practical enforcement, representative legitimacy, or equivalent outcomes.
propositions.stopping_rule: Require exact law, constituency, representative body, system, disputed action, authority, enforcement, and outcome for each transfer.

propositions.claim: APC-WORK-01 is ready for observed audit against a current cloud or AI workplace deployment.
propositions.falsifier: The action packet, update freeze, representative constitution, direct rights floor, anti-bypass, remedy, exit, or value requirements are legally or operationally incompatible in the selected deployment.
propositions.stopping_rule: Freeze one current deployment, constituency, representative body, architecture, updates, agreement, rights, outcomes, and comparator before audit.

current_result.strongest_r6_result: A representative body obtained binding function-level cessation until consent or substitute conciliation existed.
current_result.highest_supported_domain_result: bounded R6 co-governance with architecture, representation, remedy, exit, and value gaps
current_result.next_step: Audit APC-WORK-01 against one current cloud or AI workplace system with a complete works agreement, representative record, update history, worker voice, enforcement, outcomes, and R4-R7 ledger.
